🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Former Texas prosecutor and child advocate Erin Marie Benavides has died at 54.

Benavides was found dead inside her home in Port Aransas, Texas, on October 14, 2026. Police responded to a welfare concern that evening after a friend of her husband received an alarming text message from her. Officers forced their way into the home and found her with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. The Nueces County Medical Examiner's Office later confirmed her cause of death was a self-inflicted gunshot wound and ruled her death a suicide. Port Aransas police said no foul play is suspected.

Benavides was previously married to former San Antonio Spurs star Brent Barry. The two were married from 1998 until Barry filed for divorce in 2010, alleging she had an “emotional affair” with NBA Hall of Famer Tony Parker, then married to actress Eva Longoria. Benavides denied the affair.

After the divorce, Benavides built a career in law and child advocacy. She graduated from St. Mary's University School of Law in 2013 and served as an assistant district attorney in Comal and Bexar counties, as well as working with Bexar County Juvenile Probation. From 2020 to 2022, she served as president and CEO of the Youth Center of Texas, which provides crisis intervention and case management for child sex-trafficking victims. In January 2023, she joined the 38th Judicial District's anti-gang and border prosecution unit, serving Uvalde and Real counties, and resigned in August 2026.

Bexar County District Attorney Christina Mitchell paid tribute to Benavides, remembering her dedication as a prosecutor, her support for colleagues and her boisterous laugh.

Rest in Peace, Erin Marie Benavides.

If you or someone you know is struggling, call or text 988 in the U.S. to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline.

Sources: New York Post; Page Six; Uvalde Leader-News; San Antonio Express-News.
